title: Minimum Intervals to Cover a Range
statement: A city crew needs to floodlight the road segment from position 0 to position t (a positive integer). You are given a list of lamp coverage intervals, each written as [start, end] with 0 <= start <= end; a lamp lights every real point x with start <= x <= end. Return the minimum number of intervals whose union covers EVERY real point of [0, t] (endpoints included, and touching intervals such as [0, 2] and [2, 5] join with no gap at 2). Intervals may overlap arbitrarily and are given in no particular order; the same interval may appear more than once. Return the single integer count of intervals used in a smallest such selection, or -1 if no selection can cover all of [0, t]. The minimum count is unique, so return it directly.
reference_solution:
def min_intervals_to_cover_range(intervals, t):
    ivs = sorted(intervals, key=lambda iv: iv[0])
    n = len(ivs)
    count = 0
    covered = 0
    i = 0
    while covered < t:
        farthest = covered
        while i < n and ivs[i][0] <= covered:
            if ivs[i][1] > farthest:
                farthest = ivs[i][1]
            i += 1
        if farthest == covered:
            return -1
        covered = farthest
        count += 1
    return count
hints: You are building one continuous covered stretch starting at 0. At each step, which of the still-usable intervals should you commit to so future steps have the best chance?

Track the farthest point currently covered. Among ALL intervals whose start lies within that covered reach, the greedy choice is the one that extends coverage the farthest (largest end) - not simply the first one you encounter. Sort by start so you can sweep the in-reach candidates in one pass.

Sort by start. Keep covered = 0 and a forward pointer. While covered < t, scan every interval with start <= covered, remembering the maximum end among them; if that maximum does not exceed covered there is a gap, so return -1; otherwise set covered to that maximum and add ONE to the count (one extension chosen, not one per interval scanned). Return the count when covered reaches t.
